author: Kristie Ackert
title: Yankees Left Stunned as Tigers Break Century-Old Bronx Mark - NewsBreak
text:
By Kristie Ackert ,
37 minutes ago
The Detroit Tigers didn’t just beat the Yankees this week. They embarrassed them and made history in the Bronx.
And, it was a former Yankee who made sure the wound stung a little deeper.
According to OptaStats , Detroit became the first visiting team ever to win back-to-back games by 10 or more runs at Yankee Stadium. Old or new. Over a century of games, and nobody had beaten the Yankees this badly two nights in a row.
It started Tuesday with a 12–2 pounding that turned into a nightmare in the seventh inning. Casey Mize kept New York off balance for six shutout frames, then the Tigers sent 14 batters to the plate in a nine-run explosion. By the time the dust settled, the Yankees’ bullpen was cooked and the crowd booed its way into the night.
On Wednesday night, Detroit followed it up with an 11–1 dismantling. Jack Flaherty threw five shutout innings, Riley Greene and Kerry Carpenter each went deep in a five-run eighth, and the Tigers’ lineup kept hammering away.
But the loudest blow came from someone who knows Yankee Stadium all too well
Gleyber Torres was gracious in his comments and reaction to the fans in his first trip back to Yankee Stadium since leaving as a free agent last fall.
Torres ripped a two-run single in the fifth to break the game open and later added a third RBI on a groundout. Three runs driven in by the guy New York gave up on. The night after receiving a warm ovation and a video tribute, Torres gave fans something else to remember: the sight of him wearing Detroit colors while twisting the knife.
For the Tigers, these were two statement wins as they head into the playoffs.
For the Yankees, it was two nights of exposure. The shaky bullpen came back to bite them again and a lineup that is built to overwhelm teams couldn’t keep pace.
September isn’t the time to be searching for answers.
The Tigers didn’t just take a series. They took a piece of history. And Gleyber Torres made sure it hurt.
